analysis: NR2F2 regulon targets vs TSAICG GWAS loci cross-reference
result: NEGATIVE — no direct overlap, but test is uninformative due to HVG limitation

notable_targets.CALB2: Calretinin — CR interneuron identity marker (novel NR2F2→CALB2 link from Task 1313)
notable_targets.CNR1: Cannabinoid receptor 1 — major endocannabinoid target, neuropsychiatric risk gene
notable_targets.NR2E1: TLX nuclear receptor — neural stem cell proliferation, neuropsychiatric risk
notable_targets.LYPD1: Lynx1 family — nicotinic receptor modulator, cortical interneuron marker

gwas_overlap.reason_uninformative: GRN was built on 3,000 HVGs only. Zero GWAS/risk genes are among HVGs, so they cannot appear as regulon targets. This affects ALL regulons, not just NR2F2. The Fisher's exact test is structurally impossible to yield a positive result.
gwas_overlap.resolution: Requires Task 1582 (developer: targeted GRN with HVGs + TS risk genes) → Task 1584 (analyst: analyze targeted GRN)

cnr1_finding.description: NR2F2 directly regulates CNR1 (cannabinoid receptor 1) in CR interneurons. CNR1 is a major drug target (e.g., rimonabant) with neuropsychiatric relevance. While CNR1 is not in the current TSAICG GWAS gene list, it is implicated in schizophrenia, anxiety, and basal ganglia function.
cnr1_finding.therapeutic_relevance: Endocannabinoid system modulation in CR interneurons via NR2F2→CNR1 axis could be relevant to TS circuit dysfunction
